title: UPS, Backup Power, and Transfer States
summary: Interpret normal, battery, bypass, alarm, degraded, and backup-transfer states conceptually.
objectives: Interpret synthetic UPS, battery, generator, and transfer-state telemetry.
Distinguish conceptual failover reasoning from physical operation or service.

vocab.def: A modeled state in which support changes from one source or path to another.
A condition where fewer alternate components or paths remain available.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: Do not replace batteries, open cabinets, operate generators, service transfer switches, or perform energized work. Use provided telemetry only.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Compare normal, battery, bypass, alarm, maintenance, generator-available, and transfer states. A primary source becoming unavailable can lead to an alternate state, but validation evidence and qualified authorization remain necessary.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Record state transitions, expected impact, uncertainty, and escalation needs.

practice.prompt: What is a safe learner response to a UPS alarm?
practice.answer: Interpret the provided status, preserve the record, and escalate to an authorized qualified role.

quiz.question: What does a transfer state represent here?
options: A modeled change to an alternate source or path
Permission to operate a transfer switch
quiz.answer: A modeled change to an alternate source or path

reflectionPrompt: What validation would show the modeled service recovered?
